calls.reason: The claim says every AI startup loses money. TechCrunch reported in November 2025 that Gamma reached $100M ARR profitably. Full-year accounts are missing, but this credible counterexample undercuts the universal wording.

In Q1 2026 Microsoft gave an AI run rate, Google a growth percentage, and Amazon and Meta only broad segment totals; none gave a realized AI revenue total. Microsoft's testimony on past OpenAI partnership revenue is narrow and historical.
Meta's 2023 annual report puts capex at $28.10 billion, well below the $45 billion figure. So that amount would have covered at least one of the named company-years.

Both companies' 2025 cash burn is documented, with roughly $8B negative FCF at OpenAI and about $3B at Anthropic. But 'no real path to sustainability' is a judgment about the future, and breakeven targets exist that are not yet proven or disproven.
The Rao declaration gives only lower bounds: over $10B spent on compute and over $5B in revenue. Those suggest about 2:1 but neither confirm nor rule out the hedged 3:1 figure.

The claim is a sweeping judgment about viability. Data Center Watch documents Q1 2026 project delays, but no evidence measures viability across all participants, and Krutrim's reported profit is unverified.
